source.title: A Geometrical Analysis of Kernel Ridge Regression and its Applications
source.authors: Georgios Gavrilopoulos; Guillaume Lecu'e; Zong Shang

record.tranche_reason: The study proves results about multiple descents of KRR estimation error as sample size varies, using theoretical bounds rather than the original deep-network model-size experiments. This bears on V3, but it does not sweep network size or training epochs.
record.gate_note: The study reports theoretical multiple-descent results for polynomial-kernel KRR. Its results are not empirical test-error measurements. Statements about earlier work are cited results and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves its own theorems on sample-wise multiple descent for min-norm polynomial-kernel KRR. This is a different method (theory, not deep-net experiments) aimed at whether test error is non-monotone in N (V3). However, its non-asymptotic results are upper bounds only. Its sharp asymptotic result covers only the interior of each interval d^ι≪N≪d^(ι+1), where error sits at a plateau. Neither establishes that error actually rises with N, so no row can show V3's effect.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with one qualification: the non-asymptotic results are upper bounds (with an N-increasing noise term), not proofs that error rises with N. The sharp claim is asymptotic. In that regime, error minus the residual beyond degree ι is o(σξ+||f*||H) for d^ι≪N≪d^(ι+1), extending GMMM21 to sub-Gaussian designs and unifying it with LRZ20. The authors also state the results hold for λ≲1.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops theoretical upper bounds for minimum-norm polynomial-kernel KRR and studies sample-size scaling. It does not reproduce the original deep-network model-size, epoch, or data-size experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The results depend on the design distribution (sub-Gaussian coordinates versus uniform spherical design), the polynomial degree and degree-index ι, and the sample-size range. The main finite-range results concern λ=0.

fits_no_version.finding: For polynomial-kernel min-norm KRR with sub-Gaussian or spherical design, error upper bounds in each range d^ι≲N≲d^(ι+1) contain a noise term growing like σξ√(N/d^(ι+1)). Asymptotically, error equals the degree->ι residual inside each range, giving staircase-like multiple descents in N.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sample-wise multiple descent in kernel ridge(less) regression: error plateaus at successive polynomial-approximation residuals as N crosses powers of d. Theoretical upper bounds permit, but do not prove, rises near N~d^ι.

record.problems: The evidence is theoretical rather than empirical; the results concern polynomial-kernel KRR, not deep networks; the sample-size ranges and conclusions depend on stated design and kernel assumptions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were reported separately. Cited prior multiple-descent results and unrelated KRR bounds/applications were not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: No lower bound or exact error at the boundaries N~d^ι, so an actual increase of test error with more samples is not established. Deep networks are not studied.
Capacity is not varied; the axis is sample size.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across axes.

The noise term appears in the bound, and results extend to λ≲1. The study does not test whether optimally tuned regularization removes peaks, or whether the peaks are noise-driven beyond upper-bound terms.

record.verdict_notes: Reader's 'supports' label for V3 is not justified. An increasing term in an upper bound does not show increasing test error, and the sharp asymptotic result covers only the interiors of the intervals. The authors' informal claim that adding samples raises variance and error is an interpretation, not a proven lower bound. No verdict is given; the study is theoretical evidence compatible with, but not demonstrating, V3/V6-style multiple descent.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep of deep networks or test error near a model-size interpolation threshold.
The study analyzes sample-size scaling for polynomial-kernel KRR, not deep networks, and does not report empirical test-error measurements.
The study varies sample size, not capacity across model classes.
The analysis introduces a decomposition parameter k, but does not test a single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and samples.
The study does not test whether label noise or variance causes the peaks, whether optimal regularization removes them, or the stated noise/regularization dependence.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective number of parameters or test of whether that changes the curve into an ordinary U-shape.

rows.subject: minimum RKHS-norm interpolant estimator f̂₀ (KRR with polynomial kernel)
rows.size_stated: polynomial degree L; design dimension d
rows.operation_detail: Analyze estimation error as sample size N varies across degree-dependent ranges.

conditions.value: inner-product polynomial kernel of degree L
C₇₁ d^ι ≤ N ≤ c₃₄ d^(ι+1), for 0 ≤ ι ≤ L−1

rows.measure: L₂(μ) estimation error of the interpolant; the theorem also bounds its difference from the higher-degree residual term
rows.value: The stated rate r*₀,k is equivalent to max{σξ√(d^ι/N), (1/√N)||Γ≤ι f*≤ι||H, ||Γ>ι f*>ι||H, σξ√(N/d^(ι+1))}; with the stated high probability, ||f̂₀−f*||L₂ and | ||f̂₀−f*||L₂−||Γ>ι^(1/2)f*>ι||H | are bounded by a constant times r*₀,k.
rows.uncertainty: Probability at least 1−γ−γ₂−γ₁−2exp(−c d^ι)−(C₆₇/N)^(r/4), as stated in Proposition 9.
rows.locator: Section 4.1, informal Proposition 9; Supplementary Section 5.3.5, Proposition 9
rows.note: The authors present this as a multiple-descent result. The displayed rate has a term increasing with N within the stated range, as well as decreasing terms; it is a theoretical rate result, not an empirical measurement.
rows.check: Value is an upper bound on L2 error. The N-increasing term σξ√(N/d^(ι+1)) belongs to the bound, not a lower bound or the error itself, so a rise in test error with N is not shown. The state 'observed' is unsupported. The baseline correctly reads 'not stated'.

rows.subject: minimum RKHS-norm interpolant estimator f̂₀ (KRR with polynomial kernel)
rows.size_stated: polynomial degree L; design dimension d
rows.operation_detail: Analyze the asymptotic estimation error as both sample size N and dimension d grow.

conditions.value: sub-Gaussian design under the first two items of Assumption 10

rows.measure: L₂(μ) estimation error minus the norm of the residual beyond degree ι
rows.uncertainty: o_d,P(1) convergence in probability, as stated in Proposition 9.
rows.locator: Supplementary Section 5.3.5, Proposition 9, third item; Section 6.5.23
rows.note: This asymptotic result states convergence to the residual level in the interval between successive powers of d; the authors identify it as the multiple-descent regime.
rows.check: Sharp asymptotic result: error converges to the degree->ι residual within ω(d^ι)≤N≤o(d^(ι+1)). This is a constant plateau inside each interval, with step-downs across intervals. It shows descents but does not cover the transition regions N~d^ι where any rise would occur, so it cannot show 'more data hurts'.

reader_labels.condition: Polynomial-kernel minimum-norm KRR under the sub-Gaussian and spherical design settings in the stated degree-dependent sample ranges
reader_labels.reason: The authors establish multiple descents as sample size varies and give rates with a sample-size-increasing term in each stated range (r1–r3). This is theoretical evidence in KRR, not an empirical result for deep networks.
